newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still down sharply late on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still down sharply late on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained sharply lower late Monday in moderate activity, still undermined by forecasts for mostly mild U.S. weather this week that pressured the cash, industry sources said.
At 1400 EST, January tumbled 27.7 cents to $3.21 per million British thermal units, while February was 18.6 cents lower at $3.00. Others were down by two to 6.5 cents.

"Yes, the weather is pretty mild this week, but I think we may be a little overdone (to the downside) here," said one East Coast trader, noting January was off about 15 percent from its record close last Thursday.

With little extreme cold on the horizon, traders said any rally would be a real struggle, but most agreed it may be a little early for prices to collapse, with stocks still low and winter still ahead.
Technical traders pegged support in January at $3.11 and then at $3.04, with trendline buying likely in the $2.70s. Resistance was seen in today's gap between $3.38 and $3.46.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices tumbled about 30 cents Monday to about the $3.30 level, down 55 cents from December indices. Midcontinent pipes were off a similar amount to the mid-to-high $3.20s, 30 cents under December 1. New York city gate gas slipped 20-30 cents to about the $4.20 area.
NYMEX said 26,513 Hub contracts traded by 1320 EST.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas fell five cents to $1.60, while deferreds were untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX said one Alberta lot had changed hands by 1320 EST.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded at 1400 EST.
On the KCBT, January slumped 25 cents to $3.10, while deferreds were four to 17 cents lower. The East/West spread was still at 11 cents (NYMEX premium), off 2.7 cents from Friday.
